title: Characterizing diversity among human oral stem-like cancer cells using flow cytometry
protocol: Dilute collagen-I in PBS to 50 μg/mL for the required volume to cover the surface of the dish.
Incubate dishes at 37°C sterile incubator for 30 min.
Aspirate collagen solution and wash the coated surface twice with PBS.
Air dry the dishes/plates in the bio-safety cabinet.
Seal the unused plate/dishes and store at 4°C for later use.

Wash tumor sample pieces with PBS containing 2× Gentamicin, 2× antibiotic-antimycotic mix (Penicillin, Streptomycin, Amphotericin B - mix) with gentle rocking for five minutes followed by centrifugation at 500 × g for 10 s.
Wash the sample with ACK lysis buffer at room temperature (24°C–27°C) for two minutes with gentle rocking, and centrifuge at 500 × g for 10 s.
Wash twice with chilled PBS containing 2× Gentamicin, 2× antibiotic-antimycotic mix. Centrifuge at 500 × g for 10 s.
Transfer the sample in chilled tissue transport media and keep it on ice.
Put a cell culture dish on ice and transfer the sample in the dish in 500 μL tissue transport media.
Mince the sample into fine pieces using a surgical blade. Note: This minced tissue slurry should be pipettable with a 2 mL pipette.
Collect the samples and resuspend them in 5 mL of tissue dissociation media (prepared fresh and not stored).
Transfer the tissue suspension to a 15 mL tube and place it in a rack, which is placed in a 37°C water bath.

Digest the samples for 60 min with mixing by pipetting up and down using a 2 mL serological pipette with gentle pressure against the bottom of the tube five times every 15 min. Note: Keep monitoring the process of tissue digestion by taking a small portion of samples over a glass slide and checking under the microscope.
Spin at 500 × g for 10 s.
Note: This will allow undigested tissue samples to get sedimented in the bottom of the tube and digested single cells will remain in suspension.
Collect all the cells in suspension in a fresh tube (Tube A).
Wash the pellet once by adding 1 ml tissue transport media and centrifuging at 500 × g for 10 s.
Collect all the cells in suspension and add them to ‘Tube A’.
Resuspend the tumor pieces in 1 ml of tissue transport media.
Transfer 250 μl of suspension with partially digested tissue pieces to a fresh tube (Tube B) and label it as Tube B.
Set aside on ice for explant culture, as mentioned later.
Pellet the remaining partially digested tissue and add 1 ml of tissue dissociation media.
Incubate at 37°C for 10-15 min.
Pipette up and down the tissue slurry five times to check for dissociation.
Pellet down indigestible tissue parts at 500 × g for 5 min.
Collect all cells in suspension and transfer them to ‘Tube A’.
Pass the cell suspension through a 40 μm cell strainer.
Spin at 500 × g for 5 min.
Add 200 μl of ACK lysis buffer to the pellet and gently rock the tube for 1 min.
Pellet down the cells by centrifuging at 500 × g for 3 min.
Remove the buffer.
Wash cell pellets with freshly prepared chilled HBSS(+) buffer twice.
Resuspend the cells in chilled HBSS(+) buffer.
Store prepared HBSS(+) buffer at 4°C for up to 15 days.
Keep the tube on ice during preparation and handling.
Count cells in 'Tube A' with trypan blue.
Take approximately 2 × 10^6 cells from the calculated volume of cell suspension into a 15 mL tube.
Pellet down the cells at 400 × g for 5 min and resuspend in 2 mL of ALDEFLUOR™ assay buffer.
Label two separate 1.5 mL tubes as ‘unstained’ and ‘control’.
Add 500 μL of cell suspension in unstained and negative control tubes.
In the control tube, add 5 μL of N,N-diethylaminobenzaldehyde (DEAB).
Preincubate all the tubes at 37°C for 10 min before advancing to further steps.
Add 2.5 μL of activated ALDEFLUOR reagent in the ‘Control’ tube under dark condition.
Add 5 μL of activated ALDEFLUOR reagent in ‘Test’ tubes under dark condition.
Mix by inverting the tubes 5 times.
Incubate all tubes for 1 h at 37°C in a water bath.
Transfer all tubes to ice after incubation.
Centrifuge the tubes for 5 minutes at 400 × g.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend cell pellets in ice cold ALDEFLUOR™ assay buffer at a dilution of 1 × 10^6 cells per 100 μL.
Perform Fc receptor blocking using Human BD Fc Block antibody as per the manufacturer’s protocol.
Add APC-conjugated lineage antibody cocktail (in 1:5 dilution) to the ‘Test’ tube.
Add APC-conjugated human CD31 antibody (in 1:20 dilution) to the ‘Test’ tube.
Add BV421-conjugated Human CD24 antibody (in 1:20 dilution) to the ‘Test’ tube.
Add BV786-conjugated Human CD44 antibody (in 1:20 dilution) to the ‘Test’ tube.
Add isotype control antibody to the DEAB-Control tube.
Incubate tubes for 30 minutes at 4°C in the dark.
Wash cells twice with ice-cold ALDEFLUOR™ assay buffer and centrifuge at 400 × g for 5 minutes.
Pass cell suspension through a 40 μm cell strainer to collect the flow-through, avoiding any cell clumps.
Add propidium iodide at a final concentration of 2 μg/mL and incubate for 5 minutes.
Store prepared tubes only for up to 1 hour at 4°C in dark until used for flow-cytometry analysis.
For cell sorting, make collection buffer by adding 5% FBS in HBSS (+) and store at 4°C beforehand.
Collect sorted cells into appropriately labeled tubes containing collection buffer.
Phenotype analyze CD24, CD44, and ALDH-high cells using BD FACS Aria-Fusion flow cytometer.
Set gates using the strategy shown for analysis of cell populations.
Mix APC-conjugated lineage antibody cocktail with CD31-APC.
Draw a lineage antibody-negative gate for including and analyzing lineage marker and CD31-negative tumor cells.
Set forward scatter (FSC) and side scatter (SSC) dot plot to exclude debris and clumped cells.
Use unstained cells to set the appropriate voltages for FSC, SSC, and viability parameters.
Use DEAB control to set the appropriate voltages for background fluorescence parameters for APC, BV421, BV786, and Aldefluor fluorescence.
Place partially digested tissue-explants in droplets over collagen-coated cell culture plates.
Ensure droplet volume is 20-30 μL.
Monitor tissue attachment under microscope every hour.
Add extra media to cover the whole surface after attachment.
Refresh media twice a week.
Aspirate media gently when cells reach confluency for passaging.
Wash attached tissue explants with PBS twice.
Add 1 mL of pre-warmed trypsin at 37°C.
Monitor cell detachment under microscope.
Add serum-containing media to neutralize trypsin.
Collect detached fibroblast cells and grow separately in a fresh well.
Add fresh tissue explant culture media in the plate containing explants.
Allow the media to support growth of outgrowing cells from the tissue explants.
Repeat steps 56–59 of partial trypsinization to collect all outgrowing cells from the tissue explants unless the tissue is exhausted or detached, over a period of 4-8 weeks.
To enrich epithelial cells, keep repeating partial trypsinization until the epithelial cells outgrow and become the major population in the plate.
This process may take an additional 8-12 weeks for significant enrichment of epithelial cells.
Wash tissue explants with an antibiotic mix during cell culture establishment.
Monitor cell morphology and symptoms of stress in growing epithelial cells after partial trypsinization.
Re-introduce fibroblasts or keep the mixed culture for a longer period if required under stress conditions.
Transfer cryovials containing frozen cells from liquid nitrogen to a 37°C water bath.
Transfer thawed cells gently to 10 mL of plain medium in a 15 mL tube.
Centrifuge the mixture at 400 × g for 3 min.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL of prewarmed complete media.
Pre-lay 2 mL of pre-warmed complete media into a 60 mm dish.
Transfer cells to the 60 mm dish containing 2 mL prewarmed complete media.
Place the plate in a 37°C incubator with 5% CO2.
Remove media from the plate after 48 h of cell plating.
Rinse adhered cells with 2 mL of PBS to remove excess media and FBS.
Add 500 μL of room-temperature (24°C–27°C) 0.05% Trypsin-EDTA, and incubate for 5–6 min in the incubator at 37°C.
Add 1 mL of Trypsin neutralizer to the detached cell suspension.
Collect cells in a tube and spin at 400 × g for 3 min at room-temperature (24°C–27°C).
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet in 2 mL of complete media.
Count cells and plate at desired cell density for further usage.
Trypsinize cells as described in the previous section, and make single cell suspension in complete media.
Suspend cell suspension at 1 × 10^5 cells per mL in plain media without FBS.
Keep cell suspension on ice.
Take required cells to make cell suspension of 3,000–5,000 cells per mL in spheroid growth culture media containing 1× growth factor supplementation.
Make spheroid growth culture media freshly before use.
Thaw Geltrex on ice until completely liquefied, which takes at least 2 hours.
Mix thawed Geltrex at a final concentration of 1.25% with cell suspension and vortex for 5-10 seconds.
Transfer cells in the desired volume into multi-well ultra-low attachment culture plates.
Incubate seeded plates in a 5% CO2 incubator at 37°C to form spheroids over 7-10 days.
Add 200 μL of 5× growth factor supplements per mL of culture media every alternate day.
Passage primary spheroids by spinning them at 300 × g for 4 minutes.
Discard supernatant and wash spheroids twice with PBS by centrifugation to remove Geltrex.
Add 300 μL of 0.05% Trypsin-EDTA solution to spheroids.
Incubate in a water bath at 37°C for 10–15 minutes with intermittent vortexing.
Check under the microscope for complete dissociation into single cell suspension.
Add trypsin neutralizer solution and spin at 500 × g for 4 minutes.
Resuspend cell pellet in spheroid growth culture medium containing 1× growth factor supplements.
Repeat steps of primary spheroid formation (steps 73–77) for secondary spheroid formation.
